Alex / team / Elena — initial sizing note below (quick and conservative). I used Verdant's distribution and the sample traces; assumptions are listed. Spreadsheet attached (verdant_capacity_model_v2.xlsx).

Assumptions:
- Model: open-llm-13B quantized (4-bit QK kernels) as primary, FP16 13B as fallback; typical prompt length 120 tokens, chat history average 3 turns retained (KV cache hit 70%).
- Per-token service time (steady state, quantized): 0.00018s/token on an A100-80GB equiv under our runtime; FP16 path ~0.00026s/token.
- Target p95 headroom: design for 1.5x above observed steady tokens/sec to cover traffic surge and noisy tails.

Scenarios (summary):
- Steady (120M tokens/mo): average tokens/sec ~= 47 tps (sustained); design target = 47 * 1.5 = 71 tps.
- Peak 2x burst: instantaneous demand ~142 tps; plan for a 200 tps burst capacity pool for short windows.
- Month-1 onramp (20% extra): transient target ~= 85 tps.

GPU counts (A100-equivalent, conservative):
- Steady reserve: 4 GPUs dedicated (continuous) gives ~80–92 tps headroom depending on quantization mix.
- Burst pool: +2 GPUs (autoscale burst) handles to ~160–180 tps for short windows with warmed cache.
- Loss of 1 GPU group (graceful degradation): fallback to FP16 on remaining GPUs reduces tps by ~30% -> expected sustained tps ~56; fallback policy should throttle nonessential summarization jobs and route embeddings to hosted batch.

Notes: these numbers assume good KV cache hit behavior; cold-starts reduce effective tps by ~20% for initial minutes. Karthik, could you run a microbench on cache-warm vs cold numbers and paste p95 deltas?

Attachment: verdant_capacity_model_v2.xlsx

- Priyom

Quick SLO mapping and operational asks:

- p95 latency target 450ms: under Priyom's steady-reserve of 4 GPUs + 2 burst, we simulate p95 ~380–430ms assuming KV cache 70% and normal tokenizer splits. If KV drops to 40% (poorer locality), p95 drifts toward 520–580ms — we need at least one mitigation.

Mitigations I recommend (ordered):
1) Canary traffic shaping: route 30% of traffic through a warmed cache pool during first 72 hours of onramp.
2) Auto-fallback model variant: serve short prompts on a faster 6B variant (quantized) to protect tail for quick replies.
3) Set a soft throttling policy for bulk summarization jobs (batch-hosted) when node saturation > 75%.

Failure mode (single nodegroup loss):
- With current mapping, p95 spikes to ~700ms unless we immediately shift cold KV to burst-pool and enable 6B short-path. Recovery automation must be <5 minutes to avoid user-visible SLA breaches.

I'll draft a one-page runbook describing the steps (canary percentage, throttling triggers, alert thresholds). Priyom — double-check the burst pool warmup times in the sheet and add a column for expected warm cache TTL.

Marissa
Head of Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference

Ran a quick microbench as requested. Results (summary):

- Warm KV cache (steady): p95 per-request processing contribution = 260ms; cold baseline = 360ms. So warm->cold delta ~= 100ms per request under the same GPU mix.
- Cold-start tail for multi-turn chat with long history (500 tokens) adds ~120ms on average due to KV paging behavior.
- Warmup time for burst pool (spin up + model load) ~45–90s depending on quantized kernels; model load dominates. Prefetching into burst pool reduces warm cold-delta to ~40ms after first 20 requests.

Implications:
- The 2-GPU burst pool must be prewarmed ~30–60s before expected peak. For unpredictable peaks, maintain a small warm buffer (1 GPU hot) to absorb immediate spikes.
- With 4 GPUs steady + 1 hot burst GPU, we can target the p95 SLO with safer margins and <5 minute recovery if a node group fails.

I'll update the spreadsheet with the microbench numbers and include a warmup TTL column.

-Karthik
